<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Expose JSON response and SSE event schemas for chat and legacy completions in `/openapi.json`, using existing Pydantic models and OpenAPI 3.2. Related to #25272; broader client-generator issues are out of scope.

## Claims

- Both endpoints expose distinct unary JSON and SSE contracts with resolvable model references.
- SSE `itemSchema` describes an event envelope whose `data` is a JSON chunk, JSON error, or `[DONE]`. Keep-alive comments are not data events.
- Inference and stream generation are unchanged. Early disconnects now return an explicit empty `Response()` from the shared cancellation wrapper instead of `None`, avoiding response-model validation errors without making successful response schemas nullable.
- Bundled Swagger UI is updated to v5.33.1 so offline docs can load OpenAPI 3.2 documents. Rendering the SSE item schema remains an upstream limitation (see Details).

## Validation

Linux CPU checks were run by Codex at the author's request. The implementation and assertions in `b04e80127b` passed the checks below; the subsequent changes before committing only clarified test docstrings. The author confirmed validation and approved publishing this revision.

Before/after JSON captured through `GET /openapi.json` using the production routers and an in-process ASGI client, without an inference engine. These excerpts select HTTP 200 response content for the two endpoints, not the entire document. On a running server, reproduce this projection with:

```bash
curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/openapi.json | jq '
  .paths
  | with_entries(select(.key == "/v1/chat/completions" or .key == "/v1/completions"))
  | map_values(.post.responses["200"].content)'
```

Before (`4cf1307e72cb`):

```json
{
  "/v1/chat/completions": {
    "application/json": {"schema": {}},
    "text/event-stream": {}
  },
  "/v1/completions": {
    "application/json": {"schema": {}},
    "text/event-stream": {}
  }
}
```

After (`b04e80127b`; the document declares `"openapi": "3.2.0"`):

```json
{
  "/v1/chat/completions": {
    "application/json": {
      "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ChatCompletionResponse"}
    },
    "text/event-stream": {
      "itemSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["data"],
        "properties": {
          "data": {
            "type": "string",
            "anyOf": [
              {"const": "[DONE]"},
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ChatCompletionStreamResponse"}
              },
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"}
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "/v1/completions": {
    "application/json": {
      "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/CompletionResponse"}
    },
    "text/event-stream": {
      "itemSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["data"],
        "properties": {
          "data": {
            "type": "string",
            "anyOf": [
              {"const": "[DONE]"},
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/CompletionStreamResponse"}
              },
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"}
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The references resolve to generated model schemas in the same document's `components.schemas`; those definitions are omitted here. Direct payload tests check the selected models and reject malformed `choices`. Separate Schemathesis tests exercise real ASGI routes with synthetic serving-handler streams: chunks, errors, `[DONE]`, and keep-alive comments pass; malformed choices and non-JSON data fail.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_openai_schema.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_sse_keep_alive.py \
  -k 'not test_openapi_stateless' -q
```

- **40 passed, 1 deselected**, with Schemathesis 4.21.6 and FastAPI 0.136.3; also **40 passed, 1 deselected** with the minimum FastAPI 0.133.0.
- Cancellation regression: restoring the old wrapper reproduces `ResponseValidationError` on disconnect; the updated wrapper passes both disconnect and normal-completion cases.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and the additional mypy 3.12 check passed before the final docstring clarification.
- Browser checks loaded `/docs`, `/openapi.json`, and Swagger assets in online/offline modes. The OpenAPI 3.2 document loads; SSE `itemSchema` is not displayed correctly (upstream issue below).
- Existing Buildkite coverage includes the test files. The model-backed `test_openapi_stateless`, inference evaluation, and benchmarks were **not run**; the focused tests do not establish a full model-backed suite pass.

## Details

Register unary/chunk models with FastAPI; `openapi_extra` restores the unary JSON ref because the additional response model otherwise replaces it. Request structure is unchanged, but FastAPI renames `FunctionCall` to `FunctionCall-Input`; name-dependent consumers may notice.

Set the production app's OpenAPI version to 3.2.0, which defines `itemSchema`. This is a document-version change; no FastAPI dependency bump is needed. The cancellation fix is in the shared decorator and therefore applies to its other callers too; it does not change mid-stream disconnect handling by `StreamingResponse`.

**Swagger UI limitation:** v5.33.1 can load the OpenAPI 3.2 document but does not yet render `itemSchema` for sequential media types properly: [swagger-api/swagger-ui#11065](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui/issues/11065). The SSE contract is present in `/openapi.json` and exercised by Schemathesis, even though Swagger's response-schema display is incomplete. The bundled upstream assets and license are retained verbatim.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

This breaks `test_openapi_stateless`. Schemathesis validates each SSE event envelope (`{"data": "<raw string>", "event": "message"}`) against this schema, so every streaming response fails with `"model" is a required property`.

Use the shape FastAPI emits for SSE routes instead: an `itemSchema` with a required `data` string, and `anyOf` on `data` with `const: "[DONE]"`, a `contentSchema` ref to `ChatCompletionStreamResponse`, and a `contentSchema` ref to `ErrorResponse` for mid-stream errors (`contentMediaType: application/json` on both). The new unit test then reads the ref from `itemSchema`.

This turns every client disconnect into a 500. `with_cancellation` returns `None` when the client disconnects before the handler finishes. Today that becomes a 200 with body `null`. With `response_model` set, FastAPI validates `None` against the model, raises `ResponseValidationError`, and the request is logged and counted as a 500.

Smallest fix is to have `with_cancellation` return `Response()` instead of `None`. If you would rather keep it in this file, `response_model=ChatCompletionResponse | None` also works since the `openapi_extra` override hides the `anyOf`.
Same two issues as the chat router apply here.

Fixed in b04e80127b. Both endpoints now use OpenAPI 3.2 `itemSchema` for the SSE envelope, with string `data` accepting `[DONE]`, a JSON response chunk, or a JSON error through `contentSchema`. Production app construction now declares 3.2.0.

Added Schemathesis coverage through the real ASGI routes with synthetic handler streams: chunks, errors, `[DONE]`, and keep-alive comments pass; malformed choices and non-JSON data fail. The focused CPU selection passed 40 tests with Schemathesis 4.21.6 on both FastAPI 0.136.3 and the minimum 0.133.0. The model-backed `test_openapi_stateless` was not run, so this is not a claim that the full suite passed.

Also updated bundled Swagger UI to v5.33.1 so offline docs can load the 3.2 document. Swagger still does not render `itemSchema` for sequential media types properly: [swagger-api/swagger-ui#11065](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui/issues/11065). The contract is exported and validated even though that UI display remains incomplete.

Fixed in b04e80127b using your first suggestion: the shared `with_cancellation` decorator now returns `Response()` rather than `None` when disconnect wins. It still cancels the pending handler. The explicit empty 200 response bypasses FastAPI response-model validation; the successful response model remains non-nullable. This does not change mid-stream cancellation handled by `StreamingResponse`.

Added a deterministic ASGI regression test with a declared response model for both early disconnect and normal completion. Restoring the old wrapper reproduces `ResponseValidationError` on disconnect; the updated wrapper passes both cases. Since this is in the shared decorator, the fix applies to its other callers as well.

Addressed both in b04e80127b: legacy completions now export the SSE envelope through OpenAPI 3.2 `itemSchema`, and the shared cancellation wrapper returns an explicit `Response()` on early disconnect. The parameterized payload/SSE tests cover both chat and legacy completion routes; the separate cancellation regression covers the shared wrapper with a declared response model.

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("disconnect", [False, True])
+async def test_cancellation_with_response_model(disconnect: bool):
+    """Disconnect cancels work without a validation 500; success stays typed."""
+    app = FastAPI()
+    started = asyncio.Event()
+    cancelled = asyncio.Event()
+
+    @app.post("/", response_model=str)
+    @api_utils.with_cancellation
+    async def handler(body: dict, raw_request: Request):
+        """Return a typed result or wait for cancellation after reading the body."""
+        started.set()
+        if not disconnect:
+            return "done"
+        try:
+            await asyncio.Future()
+        finally:
+            cancelled.set()
+
+    messages = []
+    body_sent = False
+
+    async def receive():
+        """Deliver the parsed body, then disconnect only after work starts."""
+        nonlocal body_sent
+        if not body_sent:
+            body_sent = True
+            return {"type": "http.request", "body": b"{}", "more_body": False}
+        await started.wait()
+        if disconnect:
+            return {"type": "http.disconnect"}
+        await asyncio.Future()
+
+    async def send(message):
+        """Capture ASGI output to assert the status and serialized body."""
+        messages.append(message)
+
+    await asyncio.wait_for(
+        app(

inline_comments.body:
This breaks `test_openapi_stateless`. Schemathesis validates each SSE event envelope (`{"data": "<raw string>", "event": "message"}`) against this schema, so every streaming response fails with `"model" is a required property`.

Use the shape FastAPI emits for SSE routes instead: an `itemSchema` with a required `data` string, and `anyOf` on `data` with `const: "[DONE]"`, a `contentSchema` ref to `ChatCompletionStreamResponse`, and a `contentSchema` ref to `ErrorResponse` for mid-stream errors (`contentMediaType: application/json` on both). The new unit test then reads the ref from `itemSchema`.

This turns every client disconnect into a 500. `with_cancellation` returns `None` when the client disconnects before the handler finishes. Today that becomes a 200 with body `null`. With `response_model` set, FastAPI validates `None` against the model, raises `ResponseValidationError`, and the request is logged and counted as a 500.

Smallest fix is to have `with_cancellation` return `Response()` instead of `None`. If you would rather keep it in this file, `response_model=ChatCompletionResponse | None` also works since the `openapi_extra` override hides the `anyOf`.
Same two issues as the chat router apply here.

Fixed in b04e80127b. Both endpoints now use OpenAPI 3.2 `itemSchema` for the SSE envelope, with string `data` accepting `[DONE]`, a JSON response chunk, or a JSON error through `contentSchema`. Production app construction now declares 3.2.0.

Added Schemathesis coverage through the real ASGI routes with synthetic handler streams: chunks, errors, `[DONE]`, and keep-alive comments pass; malformed choices and non-JSON data fail. The focused CPU selection passed 40 tests with Schemathesis 4.21.6 on both FastAPI 0.136.3 and the minimum 0.133.0. The model-backed `test_openapi_stateless` was not run, so this is not a claim that the full suite passed.

Also updated bundled Swagger UI to v5.33.1 so offline docs can load the 3.2 document. Swagger still does not render `itemSchema` for sequential media types properly: [swagger-api/swagger-ui#11065](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui/issues/11065). The contract is exported and validated even though that UI display remains incomplete.

Fixed in b04e80127b using your first suggestion: the shared `with_cancellation` decorator now returns `Response()` rather than `None` when disconnect wins. It still cancels the pending handler. The explicit empty 200 response bypasses FastAPI response-model validation; the successful response model remains non-nullable. This does not change mid-stream cancellation handled by `StreamingResponse`.

Added a deterministic ASGI regression test with a declared response model for both early disconnect and normal completion. Restoring the old wrapper reproduces `ResponseValidationError` on disconnect; the updated wrapper passes both cases. Since this is in the shared decorator, the fix applies to its other callers as well.

Addressed both in b04e80127b: legacy completions now export the SSE envelope through OpenAPI 3.2 `itemSchema`, and the shared cancellation wrapper returns an explicit `Response()` on early disconnect. The parameterized payload/SSE tests cover both chat and legacy completion routes; the separate cancellation regression covers the shared wrapper with a declared response model.
